entries.title: In-person events: approve seat requests by organization, or from Slack
entries.summary: Decide a whole team's seat requests at once from **Guests → By organization**, with an optional **Seats per organization** limit. Or post requests to a Slack channel with **Approve**, **Waitlist** and **Decline** buttons; each decision records who made it and when.

where.path: Events → an in-person event → Guests → By organization; Settings → Slack approvals

entries.use_case: Teams that hand-pick a balanced room can approve or cap a whole company in one step, and the people who approve can do it from Slack without opening Sessionboard.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer approves seat requests one by one, wants to limit seats per company, or asks for approvals in Slack.
internal.who_should_get_it: Marketing customers running in-person events or tours (dinners, workshops, roadshows).
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Events → an in-person event → an in-person event → Guests → By organization; Settings → Slack approvals
internal.gotchas: Slack decisions need a Sessionboard account in the organization with the same email as in Slack. A Slack workspace already connected to another Sessionboard organization can be connected again for seat requests only; commands and mentions stay with the first organization.
internal.talk_track: Group the requests by company, approve the team in one click, or let your approvers decide right in Slack.

entries.title: In-person events: the packet in reminders, sign-up sources, moments and the after-event loop
entries.summary: Upload a packet and fill in **Getting there** so confirmation and reminder emails carry them; make a tracked sign-up link per channel and person and see sign-ups by source; get a note when the details change, the event is 80% full or it has ended; and send a thank-you with a Survey link or a no-show follow-up after the event.

where.path: Events → an in-person event → Settings → Know before you go; Follow-up

entries.use_case: Guests arrive knowing how to get there, the team sees which channel and which person filled the room, and nobody forgets the follow-up.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to send directions or a PDF to guests, which post brought sign-ups, or how to follow up after an in-person event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Marketing customers running in-person events or tours (dinners, workshops, roadshows).
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Events → an in-person event → an in-person event → Settings → Know before you go; Follow-up
internal.gotchas: Customized confirmation or reminder emails keep their words: add {{packet_url}} and {{#getting_there}} to them. Moment notes only suggest next steps; nothing is sent without a yes.
internal.talk_track: Send the packet in the reminders, know where each sign-up came from, and close the loop after the event.
